description:
Apply FieldCipher encryption to the three PII-bearing columns in the messages table. This is the highest-value encryption target: raw_message contains the full email body and headers.

## Columns to encrypt
  - raw_message   (BYTEA → BYTEA, ciphertext replaces plaintext)
  - envelope_from (TEXT  → BYTEA, encrypted, store as BYTEA)
  - envelope_to   (TEXT  → BYTEA, encrypted, store as BYTEA)

  The message subject and headers are inside raw_message and are covered implicitly.

## Schema migration
  ALTER TABLE messages
      ALTER COLUMN envelope_from TYPE BYTEA USING envelope_from::BYTEA,
      ALTER COLUMN envelope_to   TYPE BYTEA USING envelope_to::BYTEA;

  Note: this migration does NOT retroactively encrypt existing rows.
  A separate one-time migration script (not a schema migration) must be
  run to encrypt existing plaintext rows. Document this as a deployment step.

## Write path (SMTP inbound delivery, Email/import)
  1. Resolve user_id from caller context
  2. Call user_key_store.get_dek(user_id)
  3. Construct FieldCipher from DEK
  4. Encrypt raw_message, envelope_from, envelope_to
  5. INSERT encrypted bytes; discard DEK

## Read path (Email/get, Email/query, download)
  1. Fetch ciphertext rows
  2. Call user_key_store.get_dek(user_id) — one call per request, not per row
  3. Construct FieldCipher, decrypt each column
  4. Return plaintext to caller; discard DEK

## Performance note
  AES-256-GCM on a 50 KB email ≈ 50µs. One KMS Decrypt call per request
  ≈ 5–15ms (network). The KMS call dominates; row count does not matter.
  Do NOT call get_dek per row — call once per request and reuse the FieldCipher.

## Acceptance
  - New messages are stored with ciphertext in raw_message (verified by direct DB query)
  - Email/get returns the correct plaintext after decryption
  - A message inserted by user A cannot be decrypted by user B's DEK (test: swap DEK, assert error)
  - Existing tests pass
title: Encrypt messages.raw_message, envelope_from, envelope_to under per-user DEK
